editorial:
If you love disaster movies that feel real and grounded, The Wave is a must-watch. Set in the stunning Norwegian fjord town of Geiranger, the story follows Kristian, a geologist who notices warning signs that a mountain above the town is about to collapse. When it finally does, it sends a massive tsunami crashing through the narrow fjord, giving everyone just ten minutes to escape. The movie does a great job building tension before the disaster hits, and the wave itself is terrifying and well-made. The family drama at the center keeps you emotionally invested, especially as Kristian races to save his wife and son who are stuck at a hotel in the danger zone.

The acting is solid across the board, and the pacing keeps you on edge from start to finish. The special effects look surprisingly good for a smaller budget film, and the Norwegian setting adds a fresh feel compared to typical Hollywood disaster movies. On the downside, some of the dialogue feels a bit predictable, and a few side characters do not get much development. Still, if you enjoy survival thrillers with heart, this one delivers. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: After the tsunami hits, Kristian finds his wife Idun and son Sondre trapped in the flooded hotel basement. He dives underwater to reach them, and together they manage to escape before drowning. They reunite with their daughter Julia, who had been safe on higher ground with Kristian earlier. The town is left devastated with many lives lost, but the family survives. The final scene shows them together, battered but alive, as rescue efforts begin across the ruined town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves disaster thrillers and survival stories with real stakes.
